explain.say: Reaction time is the gap between something happening and you responding. For a simple task, like pressing a button when a light flashes, it is usually about a fifth of a second.

explain.say: Most of the time is spent in the brain. After the eye sends its signal, the brain must recognise the light and decide to act, and harder choices take longer.

explain.say: The order then travels down the spinal cord and along nerves to your muscles. The fastest nerve fibres carry signals at up to about 100 metres per second.

explain.say: A reflex, like the knee jerk, skips the brain completely and loops through the spinal cord, so it is several times faster. People also react a little faster to sounds than to lights.

faq.q: How fast can a person react?
faq.a: For a simple reaction to a light, most people take about 0.2 to 0.25 seconds. Reactions to a sound are slightly quicker, and reacting when you must choose between options is slower.
asks: What is a normal reaction time?

faq.q: Why does deciding take so long?
faq.a: The brain has to recognise what happened and pick the right response before sending any orders. The more options there are to choose between, the longer this takes.
asks: Why is choice reaction time slower?
Which part of reacting takes longest?

faq.q: How fast do nerve signals travel?
faq.a: Signals in the fastest, insulated nerve fibres travel at up to about 100 metres per second. Thin, uninsulated fibres, like many pain fibres, are much slower, at around 1 metre per second.

faq.q: How do you measure reaction time with a ruler?
faq.a: A friend holds a ruler above your open fingers and drops it without warning; you catch it. The farther it falls, the slower you were: a ruler falls about 20 centimetres in 0.2 seconds.
asks: What is the ruler drop test?
How can I test my reactions?

faq.q: Why are reflexes faster than normal reactions?
faq.a: A reflex loops from the sense organ to the spinal cord and straight back to the muscle, without waiting for the brain to decide. That shortcut makes reflexes like the knee jerk only a few hundredths of a second.
asks: Why does my knee kick by itself?

facts: A typical simple reaction time to a light is around 0.2 to 0.25 seconds.
In athletics, a sprinter who reacts to the gun in under 0.1 seconds is ruled to have false-started.
A dropped ruler falls about 20 centimetres in 0.2 seconds.

quiz.why: Recognising the signal and deciding what to do happens in the brain and takes the biggest share of the time.

wrong.1: The eye detects light in a few hundredths of a second.

quiz.say: A ruler falls farther before you catch it. What does that mean?
quiz.show: If the ruler falls farther, your reaction was…
quiz.why: The ruler keeps speeding up as it falls, so the longer you take, the farther it drops.

wrong.2: Distance fallen depends on time taken, so it is not the same.
